title: Free abelian normalized homology inverts simplicial homotopy equivalences
statement: Let $K,L$ be simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with simplicial maps $u:K\to L$ and $v:L\to K$. Suppose $vu$ and $\mathrm{id}_K$, and respectively $uv$ and $\mathrm{id}_L$, are joined by finite chains of simplicial maps whose consecutive terms admit a cylinder homotopy in either direction. A cylinder homotopy from $a:S\to T$ to $b:S\to T$ is a simplicial map $h:S\times\Delta[1]\to T$ with $h(-,c_0)=a$ and $h(-,c_1)=b$, where $\Delta[1]_m$ consists of order-preserving maps $[m]\to[1]$ and $c_e$ is constant at $e$. For a simplicial set $S$, let $F(S)_m=\mathbb Z[S_m]$, the free abelian group with basis vectors $[s]$ indexed by $s\in S_m$; every simplicial operator acts by $[s]\mapsto[S(\varphi)(s)]$. For a simplicial-set map $a:S\to T$ put $F(a)_m([s])=[a_m(s)]$. For a simplicial abelian group $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], set $N(Z)_0=Z_0$ and $N(Z)_m=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\ker(d_i:Z_m\to Z_{m-1})$ for $m>0$, with differential $\partial_m=d_0$ for $m>0$ and $\partial_0=0$. Write $H_m(N(Z))=\ker\partial_m/\operatorname{im}\partial_{m+1}$; a simplicial morphism $a$ induces the chain map $N(a)$ by restriction in every degree. Then for every $n\geq0$, $H_n(N(F(v)))\circ H_n(N(F(u)))=\mathrm{id}$ and $H_n(N(F(u)))\circ H_n(N(F(v)))=\mathrm{id}$. In particular $H_n(N(F(u)))$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 08P2 (lemma-homotopy-equivalence), first proof paragraph, lines 5892-5909: free homology invertibility. Finite cylinder-homotopy chains and the higher-face normalization convention are made explicit.

proof.text: Write $C(S)=C(F(S))$ for the alternating complex, with $C(S)_m=\mathbb Z[S_m]$, differential $\sum_{i=0}^m(-1)^id_i$ for $m>0$, and zero out of degree zero. The basis formulas in the statement give $F(ba)=F(b)F(a)$ and $F(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$: both sides send $[s]$ to $[b(a(s))]$ and $[s]$, respectively. Naturality with respect to faces makes $F(a)$ preserve all the kernels defining $N$, and makes $C(a)$ a chain map. Thus $N(F(ba))=N(F(b))N(F(a))$. The induced maps on homology are $[z]\mapsto[f(z)]$; chain maps preserve cycles and boundaries, so this formula is well-defined and preserves composites and identities. These observations apply also in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 08P2 (lemma-homotopy-equivalence), first proof paragraph: free abelian groups form a functor; elementary basis and cycle-quotient verification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence] in abelian groups to $F(S)$. It gives the natural chain inclusion $j_S:N(F(S))\to C(S)$ and a chain map $r_S:C(S)\to N(F(S))$ with $r_Sj_S$ and $j_Sr_S$ chain homotopic to the respective identities. Set $J_S=H_n(j_S)$. For any chain homotopy $f-g=dh+hd$ and cycle $z$, $(f-g)(z)=d(h(z))$ is a boundary; hence $H_n(f)=H_n(g)$. Applying this calculation to the two supplied homotopies gives $H_n(r_S)J_S=1$ and $J_SH_n(r_S)=1$. Consequently $J_S$ is bijective. The cited normalization is exactly $\bigcap_{i=1}^m\ker d_i$ with differential $d_0$, including $N_0=F(S)_0$; it is not being identified silently with the opposite-face convention.

source.place: Tags 019S (lemma-homotopy-s-N), normalization comparison, and 019T (lemma-homotopy-equivalence-s-N), used in 08P2. Higher-face convention supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: For a single cylinder homotopy $h:S\times\Delta[1]\to T$ from $a$ to $b$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-homotopy-free-chain-homotopy] with ring $R=\mathbb Z$. Its cylinder, constant endpoint maps, and basis-induced free chain maps are exactly those in this statement and step 1. Its conclusion gives $H_n(C(a))=H_n(C(b))$. If the cylinder runs from $b$ to $a$, symmetry of equality gives the same conclusion. No Kan or finiteness hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tags 019Y (lemma-functorial-homotopy) and 019S (lemma-homotopy-s-N), the two ingredients invoked in the first paragraph of Tag 08P2.

proof.text: Naturality of the inclusions in [lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence] gives $j_TN(F(a))=C(a)j_S$ and the identical formula with $b$. On homology these read $J_TH_n(N(F(a)))=H_n(C(a))J_S$ and $J_TH_n(N(F(b)))=H_n(C(b))J_S$. Step 3 equates their right sides. Cancelling the bijection $J_T$ from step 2 proves $H_n(N(F(a)))=H_n(N(F(b)))$ for either orientation of a cylinder. This is cancellation of explicit maps, not an assumption about naturality of the chosen $r_S$.

source.place: Tag 019S (lemma-homotopy-s-N), passage from alternating to normalized maps; natural inclusion from the cited leaf.

proof.text: Put $A(a)=H_n(N(F(a)))$. For a finite chain $a_0,\ldots,a_t$ as in the hypothesis, induct on $t$: for $t=0$ the endpoint maps are identical, and for $t+1$ the induction hypothesis gives $A(a_0)=A(a_t)$ while step 4 gives $A(a_t)=A(a_{t+1})$. Thus $A(vu)=A(\mathrm{id}_K)$ and $A(uv)=A(\mathrm{id}_L)$. Step 1 now yields $A(v)A(u)=1$ and $A(u)A(v)=1$. The first identity makes $A(u)$ injective (apply $A(v)$ to an equality), and the second makes it surjective (a preimage of $y$ is $A(v)(y)$). This proves every asserted clause for the arbitrary $n\geq0$.
